subject: Design review: BYOK offline signer for air-gapped cutover
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acme.example>
To: priyom_das@redwood.example
Cc: security@acme.example
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: BYOK offline signer for air-gapped cutover - initial ask

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for taking this on. As part of our on-prem migration we'll need to perform a cutover where the HSM used for signing will be air-gapped for the first 48-72 hours. We need a documented design for an offline (cold) signing workflow that satisfies:
- Proof of key custody for auditors (chain-of-custody notes + attestations)
- Operator separation (no single person can unseal)
- Emergency unseal / recovery path that does not rely on internet connectivity
- Minimal changes to the service side (we want the signing step as a drop-in to our existing release pipeline)

Can Redwood propose an approach that uses BYOK (customer-owned keys) with an offline signer appliance (HSM) and a network proxy for queued signing requests? Please include network topology, operator role matrix, rotation cadence, and examples of audit evidence artifacts.

I've attached our compliance checklist and the migration window. Happy to hop on a quick call later this week.

Thanks,
Oliver
Senior Cloud Security Engineer
Acme Corp

From: priyom_das@redwood.example
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acme.example>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.example, kimberly_park@redwood.example
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BYOK offline signer for air-gapped cutover - initial ask

Oliver,

Appreciate the details — attached is a first-pass design and a proposed ops checklist (see attachments). Big-picture approach we recommend:

1) Offline HSM as a signing appliance (FIPS 140-2/3 validated) located in your on-prem DMZ/ops room. Keys are generated inside the HSM during ceremony and marked as BYOK (custodial key material retained by Acme).

2) Request flow: service nodes in the VPC enqueue signing payloads to a local signing queue (RabbitMQ / SQS-compatible local broker). A small, audited proxy in the DMZ pulls payloads and presents them to the HSM via a dedicated management network. Because the HSM is air-gapped, the proxy uses an authenticated, short-lived envelope key (generated by the HSM during ceremony) to wrap requests transported on removable media or over an isolated, one-way transfer mechanism.

3) Operator & custody model: threshold-unseal with 3-of-5 operators; operator auth via hardware tokens and multi-factor backed by the customer KMS for identity assertions. All unseal operations generate an attestation file signed by the HSM which is pushed to Redwood's verification webhook (read-only) for audit capture.

4) Rotation & expiry: key rotation cadence recommended 12 months for signing keys, with emergency rotation playbook included. For short-lived wrapping/envelope keys used for transport, 1-7 day TTLs depending on network/transfer mode.

5) Audit evidence: HSM attestation blobs, PDF chain-of-custody logs, operator watch logs, signed handover receipts for any physical media. We provide templates for all artifacts.

Next steps: Soojin and Kim can follow up with a network diagram and an ops drill timeline. If this looks good, we'll prepare a rehearsed cutover runbook and a 60-90 minute pre-cutover drill with your ops team.

--
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: acme-offline-signer-requirements.pdf, proposed-cutover-checklist.xlsx

From: soojin_lee@redwood.example
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acme.example>, priyom_das@redwood.example
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BYOK offline signer for air-gapped cutover - network topology and ops drill proposal

Oliver, Priyom,

Attaching a compact network topology and a pragmatic ops drill sequence here (also uploaded to the shared drive link). Key points / rationale:

- Management network: dedicate a physically separate management NIC on the HSM host connected to an ops VLAN with strict ACLs (no general-purpose internet egress). Proxy box lives in the DMZ with dual-homed NICs: one to the ops VLAN and one to the signing queue VLAN.

- Data transfer modes:
  * Preferred: physically carried encrypted transfer (USB sealed and hashed) with signed manifest for air-gap windows.
  * Alternate: one-way data diode between signing queue and DMZ proxy when physical transfer is infeasible.

- Proxy behavior: enforces schema validation, replay protection (nonce + TTL), and writes a signed request receipt to an append-only log before handing to HSM. The append-only log is replicated to your forensic storage and to a read-only copy accessible by Redwood's audit ingestion webhook.

- Emergency unseal: pre-staged unseal shares in geographically separate safes (3-of-5) + emergency unseal table-top runbook. Emergency unseal requires on-call manager approval + two independent operators.

- Test drill: 1) dry-run key generation in test HSM, 2) envelope key workflow test, 3) end-to-end signing with physical media, 4) emergency unseal simulation, 5) post-drill evidence pack generation.

Questions for Acme: which transfer mode do you prefer (physical media vs data diode) and who are the five operator candidates so we can map to the 3-of-5 threshold for ceremony?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Principal Infrastructure Security, Redwood Inference

From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acme.example>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.example, priyom_das@redwood.example
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example, kimberly_park@redwood.example

Subject: Re: BYOK offline signer for air-gapped cutover - network topology and ops drill proposal

Thanks everyone — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few quick answers and requests:

- Transfer mode: we'll run the physical-media first, fallback to a certified data diode if the operations team flags throughput issues during the drill.
- Operator candidates: Alice Monroe (SRE lead), Ben Hsu (Infra), Carla Nguyen (Security ops), Danilo Perez (Site ops), and Evelyn Park (Compliance). We'll send the signed NDAs and operator PGP keys by EOD.

We'll book the 60-minute sync for next Wednesday. Oliver
